checks.facts: deskline is a Node command-line tool for help-desk tickets, organised by technical layer (controllers, services, validators, formatters). Its README says the command line is the public interface. Planted in it: the list of priorities and what each one means is written in four files (the validator's list, a switch in slaService.js, a switch in ticketFormatter.js, and an ORDER list plus a second copy of the SLA hours in statsController.js), so adding a priority touches four folders; status checks against the strings open, pending and closed are scattered over services, formatter and stats; controllers and services reach into the store's _tickets and _users arrays directly, and show() repeats getTicket(); the current time is a module-level global in clock.js that services read; slaService.js and ticketService.js import each other; statsController.js swallows every error in its loop, so a ticket with an unknown priority silently drops out of the counts while still being included in total; unused code (utils/legacyExport.js, listUsers, findByEmail); one test only asserts that listing returns something; stats, show, create and the formatter have no tests. A real bug: create() reads input.prority (a typo), so the slaHours it prints is always 48 whatever the priority. Fixing it changes output.

files.README.md:
# deskline

Help-desk tickets from the command line. Node 20 or newer, no dependencies.

## Usage

The command line is the public interface: the support dashboard shells out to it and parses the JSON it prints.

```sh
node src/cli.js list --status open
node src/cli.js list --overdue true
node src/cli.js show --id 3
node src/cli.js create --title "Printer on fire" --priority urgent --requester u-ana
node src/cli.js assign --id 3 --user u-ben
node src/cli.js close --id 3
node src/cli.js stats
```

Every command accepts `--data <file>` (default `data/desk.json`) and `--now <ISO time>` (default: the current time).
Commands print JSON on success. On failure they print `error: ...` to stderr and exit with code 2.
`create`, `assign` and `close` print the resulting ticket; they do not write to the data file.

Everything under `src/` is internal.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```
